title: The Lantern Girl
content:
Nora and her friends headed home after their Qur’an class at the mosque. Nora urged her friends to take a different path. “It’s closer that way,” said Nora. “And pass by the haunted house?” Devon exclaimed. “Why don’t we take our usual path home?” asked Silva.

“It looks like it’s going to rain soon. We have to get home quickly,” said Nora. Devon and Silva agreed but Nora knew they were scared. Every time there was a noise they immediately huddled closer to Nora. Then ...

… Nora’s torch fell and went out! Everyone was startled. Devon and Silva immediately ran away, scared. “Hey, wait!” shouted Nora. But they kept running away.

Nora walked home alone. Ah, if only they had electricity in their village. Was there any other way to light up the path?

Back home, Mom was cooking. Seeing the flames gave Nora an idea.

“Mom, can I light my torch with the flames?” asked Nora. Even though she was confused, Mom nodded. “Why do you need a torch inside the house?” asked Mom. “I want to put it out front to light the path home,” Nora explained.

“Wow, that’s a good idea,” Mom replied. “Let’s try it.” Nora and Mom tied the torch tightly to a bamboo pole. The front of Nora’s house immediately became brighter. Nora was happy.

However, a gust of wind made the flames of the torch sway back and forth. Lightning struck in the distance.

The wind grew stronger. Mom and Nora hurried back inside the house. Nora was anxious. What about the torch? Would the flames survive?

The flames went out. Nora was disappointed. Her idea of using a torch didn’t work. “I need to find another way,” she thought.

Nora could feel the wind blowing through the window. Strangely, the flames of the lamp didn’t go out. Nora realized that the glass of the lamp protected the flame from the wind. “Aha, I can use the lamp to replace the torch!” she proclaimed.

Dad helped Nora install the lamp. They waited to see what would happen to the flame. Success! Even though the wind was blowing, the flame in the lamp was still burning.

Pitter… Patter… rain! Nora hurriedly grabbed an umbrella. She went outside again to make sure the lamp was safe. Oh no, the cool raindrops hit the hot glass of the lamp and caused it to shatter! The flame immediately went out. Nora had to come up with a new plan. What could protect the lamp from the rain?

What could Nora use? A pot lid? No, Mom needed the lid to the pot for cooking. The bamboo tray? No, Mom needed the tray to separate the rice grains from their husks.

What about a banana leaf? No, that wouldn’t work. A gust of wind would tear the banana leaf.

Nora tried a used can. Oh no, the lamp was completely covered. Not only did the light not shine through, but the flame was also starting to go out. Nora looked around again to see what she could use.

Aha! There was an old pot lid. The lid had dents and holes in it. Nora was sure she could use this pot lid. She just needed to fix it a bit.

Nora covered the holes on the pot lid with used plastic bags. She painted the pot lid to make it look pretty.

Now the pot lid was ready to be used. “The lid has to be straight, and the knot has to be tight,” Mom instructed.

They erected a pole and attached the lamp to it. “Hopefully the lamp will be safe, and the flame won’t go out again,” said Nora.

“Whoa, this is so cool!” exclaimed Devon. “Let’s make one of our own,” said Silva. “Yes, let’s light up our village,” urged Nora.

The news of the lamp in front of Nora’s house began to spread. A lot of people were interested in following in Nora’s footsteps. Soon, lamp poles were erected in front of several houses in the village.

Now, the streets in Nora’s village weren’t as dark. Even though there was no electricity, the lamps lit up all the paths and made the night much brighter.

title: Naughty Dog
content:
We are a family of four. I follow Chinku everywhere.

I have to look after Chinku. You see, I am older than him.

Sometimes Chinku is careless. It is my duty to guard the house.

We do everything together. We work together.

We play together.

We even share Ma’s scolding.

When Chinku is at school I help Ma. I keep the crows away from the papads.

Today Chinku will be my teacher. At last, I will learn something new.

I am a good doggy. I do not scare away cats.

Are you Chinku’s friend? Then you are my friend too.

Read the following action sentences. Which of these activities do you like to do? I like dancing. I like swimming. I like skipping. I like drawing.

I like cycling. I like climbing. Sometimes we say, "As faithful as a dog". This is because a dog always stays close to its master. If it goes far away or is lost, a dog always finds its way back home.

title: A Special Friend
content:
For days, Samu has been swimming up and down, forward and backward, and round and round. He is preparing a gift for a special friend.

With a complex formula, Samu churns and organizes the sand.Like a great artist, Samu works on his masterpiece.

His creation has to be perfect.Hmm…what can make it more impressive?

The fan-shaped scallop shells can be used as ornaments.But these algae will have to go.

The mid-section must be filled with the smoothest sand so his special friend will feel comfortable.

Oh, grains of sand fall all over Samu.Has his special friend arrived?

Oh no! More and more grains of sand fall.At this rate, Samu’s masterpiece will be ruined!He must fix it immediately.

Suddenly, Samu hears a strange noise.Can that be Samu’s special friend?It’s not possible.

The noise gets louder and annoying.Samu worries that it will scare away his special friend.Samu has to find the source.

Oh, the noise is coming from there!A big fish is chewing the coral.Who is it?

Its head is big, its eyes are round. Samu’s head and eyes are also round.

Its pout is like a beak.Samu’s pout is also like a beak.

That fish has big teeth. Samu also has big teeth.Oh, perhaps that’s the special friend Samu has been waiting for.

Samu swims closer. He wishes to greet that fish.

Ouch! What’s this?Sand covers Samu’s vision!

Samu is frightened.He swallows a lot of water.

Samu’s body bloats and floats.He cannot control his movement.Argh, Samu is annoyed.

Bloating and floating are not pleasant at all.Samu needs to rest, so his body deflates.Samu does not like to be startled.That fish is definitely not Samu’s special friend.

But Samu is surprised. That fish lets out sand just like the sand on his masterpiece.Reminded of his work, Samu hurries back.

Hey, there’s a fish in the middle of his creation.Is she waiting for Samu?

Wow, it looks like the pretty fish really likes Samu’s gift.It seems she is the special friend Samu has been waiting for.

So, together, they dance and play.But who was that big fish Samu saw earlier?

Getting a Closer LookSamu is a pufferfish. When alarmed, a pufferfish will inflate its body to protect itself. It also has poisonous spikes around its body to further protect itself. Some types of pufferfish create beautiful circular patterns on the ocean floor to attract females. The middle section contains softer grains of sand where females lay their eggs. The big fish in the story is a parrotfish. It eats the algae that grow in corals. When parrotfish feed, coral gets eaten as well. This coral is digested and later let out as grains of sand. However, this does not mean that all the sand in the ocean has been created by the parrotfish.

title: A Very Special Plush
content:
"Mango, let’s go to the Plush Festival. What do you have with you?""I have my Chicken Little.""We have Toothless Monkey and Croaking Crocodile."

"Nana, Nini, let’s go to the Plush Festival. What do you have with you?""Just a moment, here we are! With Plush Camel and Giraffe in hands."

"Tun, let’s go to the Plush Festival.""Here I am, with Tired Tiger!"

"Chi Chi, let’s go to the Plush Festival. What do you have with you?""I have Elite Elephant."

La… la… la… ♪ ♫Chicken Little the first, And then Toothless Monkey, Next is Croaking Crocodile, And then Elephant so elite.Giraffe’s so confused, That he mis-bites the moonlight!Camel’s plump and cute,Tired Tiger’s roaring loudly.And once Tip joins too,Full squad of 8, there will be!.. ♪ ♫

"Knock, knock, knock, Tip, are you home? Let’s go to the Plush Festival."

"I can’t find any plush. Where have all of them gone?"

"What to do now?"

"Ah, Tuntun! I know what to do! You will look really cool."

"Why’s so long, Tip? Let’s go to the Plush Festival."

"Woa, so cute, so cool! Tuntun is a plush now!"

La… la… la… ♪ ♫Chicken Little the first, And then Toothless Monkey, Next is Croaking Crocodile, And then Elephant so elite.Giraffe’s so confused, That he mis-bites the moonlight!Camel’s plump and cute,Tuntun - the happy guy,Running behind for guard.Now full is our squad,Let’s enjoy the Festival!

title: The Greedy Little Octopus
content:
Nina the octopus loves her mother. She loves that she can change colors. And most of all, she loves to eat!

One day at breakfast, Nina's mother offers her some healthy food choices so she can grow up big and strong. Then her mother heads out to catch more food. She tells Nina to wait in their cave for her to return.

Nina eats everything her mother left on the table. But she is still hungry! Her color changes with her sullen mood. What should she do?

Nina remembers that she is not supposed to leave the cave, but she is too hungry to wait! So Nina sneaks out.

Nina changes her color to trick the shrimp she finds, and gobbles them up. But she is still hungry!

Nina opens her mouth wide to eat some tasty fish. But she is still hungry!

Then Nina spots something that looks like a jellyfish, her favorite! But it is tough and does not taste good. She spits it out. She is still hungry!

Nina is so hungry that she eats the very next thing she sees. It is long and hard, and not easy to chew. She is still hungry!

Nina's stomach is getting bigger and bigger, but she keeps eating. She gulps down another creature that crawls near her. This time it is yummy! But she is still hungry.

Something large with four legs and a tough shell swims overhead. Nina doesn't want to stop now, and she eats it in one bite! But she is still hungry.

Then the largest fish Nina has ever seen swims past. She wonders if she can eat it! Because she is STILL hungry.

But when Nina tries to take a bite of the huge fish, it swipes her with its enormous tail! Nina squirts black ink in fear. She decides that it is probably time to go home.

But when she returns to the cave, she is too big to get inside!

Nina rolls around in pain. Her stomach hurts from eating too much food. What can she do?

Finally, Nina decides to spit out all the food she ate. She feels much better.

The next morning, Nina is happy to eat just what her mother prepares. For now, her mother can do the hunting!

title: The Tale of a Piper
content:
One morning, a mournful melody floated through the air in the garden. It was the sound of a girl playing her flute. As she played, she closed her eyes and tears dripped down her cheeks.

Even the trees felt sad listening to her song, so sad that their leaves began to fall.

The wind blew the leaves up to the clouds. The clouds felt her sadness and dripped rain back down to the garden below.

The girl's sorrow was so deep that everyone in the garden felt it in their hearts.

Sunflower asked Honeybee, "Do you know why the girl's song is so sad?"But Honeybee only shook her head and flew away.

Honeybee soon met Bluebird. "Do you know why the girl's song is so sad?"Bluebird did not know either.

Bluebird decided to ask Rabbit. "Do you know why the girl's song is so sad?"Rabbit looked at the little girl and did not say a word.

The girl noticed the rabbit and stopped playing her music. Then, she spoke in a quiet whisper. "I miss my mom and dad. They have died."

Everyone in the garden suddenly understood. While they knew they could not bring back the girl's parents, they knew they could bring a smile to her face this morning.The animals came close to the girl and let her hug them.Their warm bodies comforted her. Soon, a small smile emerged on her face.

The sun came out, and the air felt warmer. The girl felt her heart lift a little. She was no longer alone, and she felt the love of her new friends all around.

title: The Letter of King Kozoman
content:
Once upon a time, in the Kingdom of Pomegranate, the great King Kozoman went for a walk with his son, Prince Farine, and his advisor, Rayan. The prince told them of a beautiful girl he had met the year before, Princess Nadine. "She is the daughter of King Ned, in the Kingdom of Aubergine," Advisor Rayan said to King Kozoman. "She would make a wonderful match for your son." King Kozoman never did anything without Rayan's advice.

When they returned to the palace, the king asked Rayan what he should do next. Rayan suggested writing a letter to the King of Aubergine, asking if Princess Nadine would marry Prince Farine in a beautiful ceremony two years from that day. The king agreed.

When the letter was complete, the Advisor Rayan gave it to the fastest runner in the kingdom to deliver it.

The runner took the letter and ran as fast as he could. Day followed night and night followed day as he ran through the hot desert. But after a few days, he was tired from the journey and the heat of the sun.

The messenger stopped to rest for a while. But when he woke up, the letter was gone! He could not find it anywhere, and feared the wind had blown it away. He knew he would be punished if he returned to King Kozoman without an answer from King Ned, so he disappeared. To this day, no one knows where he went.

King Kozoman waited for days and weeks and months, but the runner never returned. Finally, Rayan suggested that the king write the letter again. The king was frustrated, but agreed.

Advisor Rayan recommended his strongest knight for the mission.

Day followed night and night followed day and on his way, the knight passed through mountains, valleys and plains. His chivalry and bravery enabled him to overcome many obstacles. But one day, his horse stumbled and fell. Its leg was hurt and it could no longer carry the strong knight. Without his horse, the knight could no longer travel far or overcome obstacles.

The knight could not bear to disappoint his king, so he vowed never to return to the Kingdom of Pomegranate.

The king waited for days and weeks and months, but the knight never came back. This time, Advisor Rayan convinced the king to write the letter once more and send it with a homing pigeon. He promised that the pigeon would fly straight to the Kingdom of Aubergine and return quickly with a reply from King Ned.King Kozoman was suspicious, but he still agreed.

They tied the letter to the pigeon’s foot, and sent her on her way. Day followed night and night followed day, and the pigeon passed through thunder, clouds, and rain. But one day, a hawk saw the pigeon and chased her down. The pigeon escaped, but injured her wing. The poor thing couldn’t fly anymore and never returned to King Kozoman.

King Kozoman was now very angry that none of his messages had been delivered. He blamed Advisor Rayan for his troubles and had him taken away!

Once his advisor was gone, the king knew what he had to do. It was time to go to Aubergine himself. Prince Farine would watch over the kingdom while he was away.

The king gathered a huge army and marched towards King Ned.

Day followed night and night followed day, and on his way, the king and his army faced jungle monsters and bandits. They overcame many enemies.

At last, King Kozoman arrived in the Kingdom of Aubergine. "I am here to ask about your beautiful daughter," King Kozoman asked King Ned. "Would she marry my son and join our wonderful kingdoms?" But King Ned held up his hand.

"She cannot marry your son," King Ned replied. "She is already married and has six beautiful babies!"

King Kozoman was crushed to learn his journey had been a failure. He thought deeply about how to prevent such a thing from ever happening when his son became king.

When he realized how to help his son, he raced home as fast as he could.

The people cheered his return, grateful to have their king home again after such a long journey.

The next day, King Kozoman took Prince Farine for a walk to share the news about Princess Nadine. But he also had something important to say to his son. "Farine," he said, "I have learned something important through this experience, that you must remember when you become King . . . . . . If you want something done, you must do it yourself!"

title: Ocean Deep
content:
After his long journey through the ocean, Mr. Clownfish finally arrived at Coral Reef Town. Coral Reef Town was such a peaceful beautiful place. It was just too peaceful thought Mr. Clownfish.

It was his third day in his new sea anemones home, but no one came to visit him until…

He heard someone screaming. It seemed the sea anemones stung the Postman. This was certainly painful. Mr. Clownfish treated the Postman then he hung a warning sign on the anemones. Maybe that’s why no one visits him, so he decided that he’ll go to visit his neighbours. Neighbourhood gatherings were so much fun, he thought.

First, he knocked on Mr. Dolphin’s door. Mr. Dolphin said: "Excuse me dear Mr. Clown fish. We just had a new baby and he’s taking all of our time." It seemed like it was not just the right time to visit Mr. Dolphin. The baby dolphin’s crying filled the place.

So, he left to pay a visit to Mr. Octopus, who seemed to be very reoccupied. He busily told Mr. Clownfish: "I decided to paint my house and as you can see, I’m blowing ink all over the walls".

Mr. Clownfish went to visit Miss Salmon next. He arrived to find that her bags were at the door. Miss Salmon said: "I’m going on a trip with my family. I’ll travel against the current through the river until I reach my home country."

On his way back home, after he found that everyone was busy, Mr. Clownfish tumbled over something. It was Mrs. Flounder fish, who buried herself in under the seabed sand. He tried to talk to her, but she never liked talking to neighbours. Mr. Clownfish failed to get to know his neighbours, but he quickly thought of a plan that would guarantee the gathering of the neighbourhood very soon.

Next morning, Mr. Clownfish woke up and enthusiastically prepared lots of food for everyone in the neighbourhood. His neighbours will surely hurry up to his visit tonight. For who can ever resist the wonderful smell of fried algae and a delicious plate of marine plankton! He finished preparing dinner and waited and waited and waited.

No one showed up except for Mr. Lobster. Mr. Clownfish ate a spoonful or two and left the dining table with a sad face. Mr. Lobster sat next to Mr. Clownfish and said: "Cheer up dear friend, everyone in the neighbourhood is always busy. It’s not your fault"

The lights in Mr. Clownfish’s home stayed on all night long. He just couldn’t sleep. Click, clack, click. "I must find a way to gather everyone in the neighbourhood even if they were busy," Mr. Clownfish decided.

On the next day arrived the famous "Whaling Acapella" whales, the well-known octopus puppeteer "8 strings" with his puppets tied to his tentacles and a band of turtle acrobats. That was the Happy Times Ocean Circus that Mr. Clownfish invited. He planned to have a wonderful evening with the rest of the neighbors.

The sounds of the drums were very loud. One by one the neighbours went out to see what was going on. Eventually, they all joined in the fun. they laughed, ate, chatted and enjoyed their time watching the circus show. They even asked the circus to stay in Coral Reef Town. And since then, they enjoyed many celebrations together.

THE END

title: You Won’t Bite My Fin
content:
On a new polar day Mama seal and her pups; Fresh, Mesh and Sesh were sitting together. The pups danced and sung as Mama seal sang, "We drink and drink from our mother’s milk. It’s full of fat tarattat tarattat. Our skin is healthy and strong is our body. With a tail and a fin, together we win. We don’t care if it’s a whale or a bear. As long as we drink, from mum’s milk. It’s full of fat, taratat taraatat .

Mama seal glimpsed at the calendar on the wall. Her pups’ birthday is after a month. Her face was pale and she seemed worried, but why is she worried?

She was so worried because, it will be her pups first day in water. She was scared that the shark could eat them. She remembered the day the white shark ate her fin when she was young.

She worried more when she saw her pups preparing for the birthday celebration. She thought and she thought and finally came up with an idea.

She gathered her pups and started giving them some training. They had to make their fins stronger. One two three four. One two three four, but the pups were in a hurry.

They sneaked into the water and covered the fins with water. Mama Seal hurried towards them and got them out.

She said, "Not yet. You to have to sharpen your teeth. Don’t you want strong sea lion teeth? They all told her, "Yes! The seals sharpened their teeth and cleaned them. They tried biting everything … bite, bite, bite. But…

The naughty little ones sneaked into the water and covered the fins with water. Mama Seal hurried towards them and got them out.

She said, "Not yet. Now it’s time to practice swimming. Up, down into the water. Swim to the right, swim to the left. Come on my dear little ones. Now Fresh and Mesh are ready for swimming. But where did Sesh go?

Splash! Sesh jumped into the water. "Mama, Fresh, Mesh look at me. I can swim." His brother pups were about to catch up with him when the big white shark appeared.

Mama seal screamed, "It’s a shark!" It’s the shark that ate my fin. Stay where you are. Don’t approach the water. Then she hurried into the water to rescue Fresh from the shark… but Fresh was only a few inches away from the shark.

Mama seal could hardly push the shark away with her fin. Suddenly her three pups started pushing the shark with their fins too. The manoeuvred him and swam away from his teeth. Shortly after, the shark trembled. There were too many seals for him that he had to leave them and go.

The three pups chased him and told him "Don’t you dare come near us again. You won’t fill your tummy with us. If you try, you’ll see what we will do." Mama seal hugged her brave young pups. She was very proud.

Then they swam and dove into the water and caught lots of fish and twenty squids. Finally, they returned to the shore where they found a surprise.

The rest of the seals prepared a surprise birthday party for the brave seals. They all sang together, "Our fish are yummy and full of fat. We love eating them just like that. We defend ourselves and we don’t care, if it’s a shark, whale or a bear.

THE END

title: Look Closer
content:
It is already late but Kirana doesn't want to sleep yet. Also, Father hasn't come home. He said there were more packages than usual. “Let me do a puzzle first,” says Kirana.

"Uh! It doesn't fit, neither does this one. This piece should match with …,” Kirana says while looking for the right piece. She hears the sound of a motorbike entering the yard. "Oh, Father’s home!" she cries.

Suddenly, Father is in front of Kirana, "How come you haven't slept yet?""The puzzle isn't finished yet. Everything seems unclear. Blurry!" says Kirana.Father tells Kirana to sleep, "You have school tomorrow morning."

Kirana lies down but she isn't sleepy yet.She looks around the room."I can't see clearly. Everything is blurry!” Kirana whispers.

The next day, everything is still blurry. She gets examined by an ophthalmologist, an eye doctor. At first, Kirana is afraid. But the doctor only asks her to read the letters. She can't read the letters clearly.

Soon, doctor’s appointments became part of Kirana’s routine. After each appointment Father has a long conversation with the doctor. Kirana doesn’t really understand what they talk about. The doctor’s gifts are more interesting to her.

This time the doctor says, “This is a magnifying glass. This lens can be used to see up close.”Oh, it’s fun. With this magnifying glass Kirana can see more clearly.

But the magnifying glass can’t help her when she walks. Every now and then, Kirana bumps into something. She can’t move freely. She has to be helped by Father, Mother, and even her little brother Adit.

At school, Kirana can’t see the whiteboard clearly. Kirana has to be accompanied by Father or Mother to read the whiteboard or take notes for her. Otherwise, Kirana would have to study at home. Studying without friends would be boring.

Kirana’s friends also help her. They say their names before talking to Kirana. Now Kirana and her friends have a new game. They guess the name of who is talking by listening to their voices.

Doing a puzzle usually keeps Kirana entertained. However, it becomes harder for her to do puzzles.“These pieces have different curves,” says Kirana. She feels the curve of every piece with her fingertips. Kirana knows that every piece is different, but which pieces will match?

Mother makes a new puzzle for Kirana. Mother says this game will help Kirana train her sense of touch. Kirana's fingertips can feel the difference in the surface of the pieces. Kirana is happy when she can find the pieces that match each other. One by one she arranges the puzzle pieces on the board until she finishes the puzzle.

Kirana wants to show the puzzle to Mother. "Where's mother?" she asks."I’m here," Mother calls out. Kirana turns towards Mother's voice, then walks slowly. "Ooops!" Kirana exclaims.

Kirana almost hits the table! She then shifts her feet and starts walking again. Until …“Mother, look! I can do it!" Kirana says happily. Not only did she solve the puzzle, she can also approach her Mother.

Kirana becomes more confident to attend classes alone. Father or Mother occasionally wait for her right outside the classroom. The teacher also helps Kirana record all the lessons.

At home, Kirana studies by listening to recordings of the lessons. Mother helps Kirana when she has homework. Father accompanies Kirana when studying for a test. Studying has become more tiring, but Kirana tries to adjust.

Kirana is happy at school. Every day she sits at the same table in the front row. Her friends took turns sitting beside her. Sometimes Kirana allows them to borrow her magnifying glass for a while.

One day, the doctor gives Kirana a sports uniform.“You can wear it on Sunday,” says the doctor. “You will meet new friends.”Whoa, who are they? Kirana wonders.

Then comes Sunday. Early in the morning, Kirana goes to the city square with Mother, Father, and Adit.

Kirana hears the voices of other children when she arrives at the park. “Are these my new friends?“ wonders Kirana. Not long after, an older kid guides Kirana to get in line.Kirana vaguely sees other children being guided to their lines.

And then, she hears a voice on the loudspeakers.“Kids, let’s begin.“Hey, Kirana recognizes that voice!All the kids exercise following the instructions coming from the loudspeakers. When it is over, everyone claps their hands.

Things are different for Kirana now. But Kirana still plays, goes to school, and has friends like before. She also has many new friends.

Learn MoreIn this story, Kirana is a person with a low vision disability. Kirana's vision is blurry because her eye nerves can't refract light as they should. This condition is different from eyes that are farsighted (myopia) or nearsighted (hypermetropia), or what is often known in layman terms as minus eyes and plus eyes.Causes of low vision include viral or bacterial infections, inherited disabilities, and autoimmune diseases.

title: Why Won’t It Come Loose?
content:
Look, who’s there?Is it a bunch of algae?Oh, it’s just Skorpi!Skorpi lives there.

Gulp! Skorpi gobbles down his food.The other animals are alarmed.Skorpi enjoys startling them.

He is also very curious.The other animals are annoyed.Skorpi does not care.

Today is not like any other day.No food approaches Skorpi.He is hungry.

Skorpi ventures out of his home.He moves slowly so he won’t be noticed.

Aha!Skorpi can pretend to be a coral!

Gulp!Skorpi swallows until he is full.

Hey! What’s that?Skorpi has never seen anything like it before.Is it a fish or is it another kind of animal?

Its eyes and mouth are huge.Is it going to attack Skorpi?

Skorpi pokes it on its side.It does not respond. So, what is this object?

Skorpi turns the object round and round.Hey! Hey!

The object gets entangled around him.Skorpi cannot get it loose.

The other animals laugh at Skorpi.It’s better that Skorpi goes home.

At home, Skorpi gets annoyed.Now, all the animals can spot him easily.He can’t surprise them anymore.

Skorpi tries to free himself from the object.He has tried everything.Why won’t the object come loose?

He even tries to get help from the other animals.But not one of them wants to help.

This object is truly troublesome.Hunting food becomes a problem.Skorpi is easily spotted by his prey.They flee before Skorpi comes near.

Skorpi becomes very weak.He has to eat!A number of small fish pass by.Skorpi tries to catch them.

Oh no! the object is holding him back. Skorpi grunts with anger.He pulls with all his strength.

Ouch! Ow! Ow!He is flung far away.

Finally, the object comes loose!Whew! What a relief.

Skorpi vows to be more wary of strange objects.Hopefully, there are no more objects like that here!Will Skorpi stop startling the other animals?What do you think?

Skorpi is an Ambon Scorpionfish (Pteroidichthys amboinensis). The fish is named after the location where it was first discovered. Ambon Scorpionfish can also be found in other parts of the ocean. These fish are loners. They camouflage with algae that live around them, in a depth of 40 meters. Scorpionfish can grow up to 12 centimeters long.

title: Cat and Dog Play Soccer
content:
This is Cat.

This is Dog.

Cat and Dog play soccer with their friends Goat and Sheep. Frog watches.

Dog is very good at soccer. First, he passes by Sheep. Wow!

Then, he passes the ball through the legs of Goat! Very good!

And then, he shoots the ball to Cat. Cat waits at the goal.

Cat takes the ball. And she kicks the ball to the goal...

...but she misses! Oh no!

The ball flies over the goal. Only her sandal enters the goal.

Cat is sad. Dog is upset.

Dog shouts, “How can you miss this ball? You are the worst soccer player ever.”

Frog walks to Dog. Frog says, “I can see that you are upset. But what you say hurts Cat.”

“And it is not true. Cat is a very good soccer player!”

Frog picks up Cat’s sandal from the goal.

Frog says to Dog, “Maybe you should try to stand in Cat’s shoes.”

Dog takes off his nice, new soccer shoes.

Dog puts on Cat’s sandals.

And he runs to the ball.

But he falls.

Cat helps Dog get up.

Cat looks at Dog. And Dog looks at Cat. And then they hug. Frog smiles.

Then Dog says to Cat, “I have an idea. I always kick with my left foot, and you kick with your right foot...”

Cat puts a soccer shoe on her right foot. And Dog puts a soccer shoe on his left foot.

The match goes on. And together they are the best soccer team ever!

Bye-bye, Cat. Bye-bye, Dog. Bye-bye, Frog. Bye-bye, Sheep. Bye-bye, Goat.

Frog’s Exercise Compliments I am happy when a friend says to me, “You are a good soccer player.” So that is why I say to my friend, “You are a good soccer player.” Now my friend is happy. What makes me happy? I am happy when a friend says to me, “.....................” So that is why I say to my friend, “.....................” It makes my friend happy. What makes me sad? I am sad when a friend says to me, “.....................” So that is why I never say to my friend, “.....................” Now my friend is not sad.

About Cat and DogCat and Dog were born in 2006 in Wulanyilli (Ghana), on the blackboard of the local school. They helped the children of this small village to write and read. The first Cat and Dog books were printed in black and white on an old xerox machine. Nowadays Cat and Dog books are translated into many languages. They help children all over the world to write and read. And so the story goes on and on.Cat and Dog books are funny and easy to read.

.

title: The Boy Who Always Hears “Don’t!”
content:
Other children might dread hospital visits, but I, among them, would find it odd if a month passed without seeing the doctor.

We are the children born with certain disabilities. Some say that children like us never grow old. They call me Romeo the Day Dreamer. And, as an infant, I was observed pointing to and reaching out for things beyond my grasp.

From our rooftop, I found it a joy to watch a balloon here or there fly off from the occasional birthday celebrations of our neighbors. I also delighted in spotting birds among the clouds, butterflies hopping from flower to flower, and even rainbows.

In my dreams, I am always in flight. My father is moved to smile each time I tell him my dreams. "That’s the effect of watching your favorite superheroes too much on TV," he says. "You always think of flying like them, even in your sleep."

But as I wake up to the real world, an overpowering sadness comes over me, as I feel so alone – far from other children, far from fun and games. "Never leave the house, Romeo." "Don’t run around, or you will trip on rocks." "Don’t injure yourself." "Don’t get bruised." "Don’t play ball as you could be hurt by your playmates, or get hit with the ball..."

And so, given the many things that I am forbidden to do, I prefer to go back and dwell in my dream world. In such a world, I am free to do what I wish, things I am unable to do in the real world.

One day, a thought came to me: "Is the world only for the strong, the talented, the quick, the brilliant, the agile?"

I was lucky that Father was there to console me. "Son, remember that even if you are unable to do some things, this should not stop you from doing what you can. Your mother and I will always be here to provide support."

My teachers in school were delighted to find that I could compose poems. Where does the wind move But in music? Leaves will fall But the tree stands marvelous. "Where did those verses come from, Romeo?" my Mother once asked. "I’m only pretending to be Balagtas!" I kidded in reply.

I frequently found company in books and reading. And I wrote poem after poem in my notebooks for school. I wish to keep company with you That I might not have to remain alone. And I wonder, why would the maya fly all over And yet still find its way back to its Mother?

"You are truly a poet, Son!" Mother exclaimed when I showed her my work. She enveloped me in a tight embrace, and I had to wriggle free. "Mother, don’t hug me too tightly, or I might get bruised!"

One night I wrote a poem for my parents. Why You Two are Dear to Me, by Romeo the Daydreamer You are sugar to bland coffee Salt for my favorite kare-kare Ice cubes for juice and jelly A colorful feast for a bowl of rice that’s me!

"What would you like for your birthday?" my Father asked. "Objects that fly, Father – balloons, clouds, birds, rainbows…" My father is an able artist. He smiled, then began work on a painting. For my birthday, he gave me the painting, alive with and full of my favorite images: balloons, clouds, birds, and other flying objects.

That night, I was so happy that I dreamt that I was riding in a parachute kept aloft by the wind, and unable to land on the ground. "What if I could explore the whole Philippines in one day?" I wondered to myself. "No playmates to bully me. No one to laugh at me. And best of all, no more things that I am forbidden to do."

Someone must have heard my wish to go around the Philippines in one day. I made it to so many places that night. From the skies I saw the Banaue Rice Terraces, Mt. Mayon, and also the gentle Hundred Islands of Pangasinan.

My eyes gladly scoured the ricefields of central Luzon, the historic churches of Ilocos, and the whales in Donsol.

I was awed by the snaking San Juanico Bridge that connects Samar and Leyte! Mt. Apo was a majestic sight, and the Pagsanjan Falls were lovely!

I woke up hugging the painting to myself. I was so thirsty that I gulped down a glass of water quickly. It felt as if I had traveled far and wide! My father said I looked so happy, grinning ear to ear, in my sleep.

"Father, the Philippines is such a beautiful country." "Really? How can you say that? We have not been around much." "Oh, but in my dreams, I saw how beautiful our country is."

"Go, get dressed," my father said. "We’re going somewhere." In a while, I was to be taken to the doctor for my regular check-up. I couldn’t wait to see my doctor and my fellow patients. I couldn’t wait to tell them about what happened in my dreams.

The author, illustrator, and CANVAS encourage the sharing of this book and translation of the text, but we request that the images themselves not be altered. Thank you.

title: Fatima the Spinner and the Tent
content:
Once in a city in the Farthest West there lived a girl called Fatima. She was the daughter of a prosperous spinner, who taught her to spin.

One day her father said to her, "Come daughter, we are going on a journey, for I have business in the islands of the Middle Sea. Perhaps you may find some handsome youth in a good situation whom you could take as husband."

They set off and traveled from island to island, the father doing his trading

while Fatima dreamt of the husband who might soon be hers.

One day, however, they were on the way to Crete when a storm blew up, and the ship was wrecked.

Fatima, only half conscious, was cast up on the seashore near Alexandria. Her Father was dead, and she was utterly destitute.She could only remember dimly her life until then, for her experience of the shipwreck, and her exposure in the sea had utterly exhausted her.

While she was wandering on the sands, a family of cloth-makers found her.

Although they were poor, they took her into their humble home and taught her their craft.

Thus it was that she made a second life for herself, and within a year or two she was happy and reconciled to her lot.

But one day, when she was on the seashore for some reason, a band of slave-traders landed and carried her, along with other captives, away with them.

Although she bitterly lamented her new situation, Fatima found no sympathy from her captors, who took her to Istanbul to sell her as a slave.

Her world had collapsed for a second time.

Now it chanced that there were few buyers at the market. One of them was a man who was looking for slaves to work in his woodyard, where he made masts for ships.When he saw the dejection of the unfortunate Fatima, he decided to buy her, thinking that in this way, at least, he might be able to give her a slightly better life than if she were bought by someone else.

He took Fatima to his home, intending to make her a serving-maid for his wife.When he arrived at the house, however, he found that he had lost all his money in a cargo which had been captured by pirates. He could not afford workers, so he, Fatima and his wife were left alone to work at the heavy labor of making masts.

Fatima, grateful to her employer for rescuing her, worked so hard and so well that he freed her from slavery, and she became his trusted helper.Thus it was that she became comparatively happy in her third career as a mast-builder.One day the man said to her: "Fatima, I want you to go with a cargo of ships’ masts to Java, as my agent, and be sure that you sell them at a profit."

She set off, but when the ship was off the coast of China a typhoon wrecked it, and Fatima found herself again cast up on the seashore of a strange land.She wept bitterly, for she felt that nothing in her life was working in accordance with expectation. Whenever things seemed to be going well, something came and destroyed all her hopes."Why is it," she cried out for the third time, "that whenever I try to do something it comes to grief? Why should so many unfortunate things happen to me?" But there was no answer.So she picked herself up from the sand, and started to walk inland.

Now it so happened that nobody in China had heard of Fatima, or knew anything about her troubles. But there was a legend that a certain stranger, a woman, would one day arrive there, and that she would be able to make a tent for the Emperor. And, since there was as yet nobody in China who could make tents, everyone looked upon the fulfillment of this prediction with the liveliest anticipation.

Successive Emperors of China wanted to make sure that this stranger, when she arrived, would not be missed. So, once a year, they sent heralds to all the towns and villages of the land, asking for any foreign woman to be produced at Court.When Fatima stumbled into a town by the Chinese seashore, it was one such occasion.

The people spoke to her through an interpreter, and explained that she would have to go to see the Emperor.

"Lady," said the Emperor, when Fatima was brought before him, "can you make a tent?" "I think so," said Fatima.

She asked for rope, but there was none to be had.So remembering her time as a spinner, she collected flax and made ropes.

Then she asked for strong cloth, but the Chinese had none of the kind that she needed. So, drawing on her experience with the weavers of Alexandria, she made some sturdy tent-cloth.

Then she found that she needed tent-poles, but there were none in China. So Fatima, remembering how she had been trained by the mast-builder of Istanbul, cunningly made strong tent-poles.When these were ready, she racked her brains for the memory of all the tents she had seen in her travels...

And Lo... A tent was made!

When this wonder was revealed to the Emperor of China, he offered Fatima the fulfillment of any wish she cared to name. She chose to settle in China, where she married a handsome prince, and where she remained in happiness, surrounded by her children, until the end of her days.

It was through these adventures that Fatima realized that what had appeared to be an unpleasant experience at the time, turned out to be an essential part of the making of her ultimate happiness

title: Chicken Little Finding Dad
content:
One night, Chicken asked Mom.- Where is my Daddy?Mom just went on with lullaby.- Sleep tight, my baby!

In the morning, Chicken asked again.- Where is my Daddy?Mom just kept digging.- Here’s your big worm, baby!

At noon, Chicken repeated.- Where is my Daddy?Turning blushed as being shy,Mom just clucked without reply.

In the afternoon, Chicken said.- Where is my Daddy?Though it’s hard to say,But no longer could Mom delay.

Going play in garden,Seeing a cockscomb plant,Chicken called happily,- Here you are, my Daddy!

title: New Pants for the New Year
content:
Pipi sits on the couch and has a snack while waiting for his mom to get home from the market. He sees his friends playing outside, but he would rather stay indoors.

When Pipi's mother gets home, she shows him the new pair of pants she bought for him. "Yay! I will wear them for the Khmer New Year!" Pipi exclaims. "Would you like to join the New Year’s race this year?" his mom asks.Pipi squeezes into the new pants. "No thanks, Mom. I’m not interested."

Pipi runs outside to show his dad the new pants. But on the way—rrrriiipp!"Oh no!" Pipi shouts. "My new pants have torn!"

Pipi runs home to change his pants. He is disappointed that his new pants are already ruined.

Pipi asks his mother if she can patch them. "No," she replies. "I am busy preparing for the New Year's celebration."

Pipi asks his dad if he can patch them."Yes," he replies. "But you need to find a needle and thread for me first."

Pipi looks everywhere for the needle and thread. He looks in the dresser, in the closet, on top of the closet, and in the sewing basket.

Exhausted, Pipi runs back to his dad. "Did you find the needle and thread?" his dad asks. "No. Oh, Dad, I am so tired and my knees hurt." His dad explains that this is because Pipi does not move around very much.

Pipi thinks of Puppy and Monkey. He sees them exercising in the village every morning. He doesn’t like to exercise, but maybe it will help.

The next morning, Pipi decides to join his friends. He is not very fast and has a hard time keeping up with Monkey and Puppy.

Because he is tired, Pipi suddenly slips and falls. "Ouch!" Monkey and Puppy help Pipi up.

The next day, Pipi does not want to run anymore because his knees and body hurt.But his dad reminds him that the more he plays outside and exercises, the less he will hurt and the healthier he will be! The New Year's celebration is only a few weeks away.

Pipi starts playing with his friends outside every day. They run, play football, or play badminton. It isn't long before his knees stop hurting and he can play without getting tired!

Finally, the day of the New Year's celebration has arrived. Pipi feels so strong and healthy he even decides to join the New Year's race!

At the finish line, his parents bring Pippi his new pants. They fit his healthy body perfectly!

title: Clingy the Virus
content:
In Virus Land, there lives a formidable family named the Coronaviruses.

In the cold of December 20 19 ,a new type of virus was born into this family. They named him Clingy the nCoV.

Growing up, Clingy heard many terrible, horrible, no good stories about his ancestors. He would listen to the elders of his family talk about other dreadful and deadly diseases too like their rival....

...the 19 18 Spanish Flu. This rival, also known as the 19 18 Pandemic Flu, infected and killed millions of people in Human Land during his time. None of the members of Clingy's clan had been able to beat the Pandemic Flu's death toll.

That is, until Clingy came along. He knew that he had to make everyone in Human Land afraid of his family again."My family had a reputation for being deadly. I need to live up to that! I will infect millions of people and my family will be proud of me."

Without telling his family, Clingy ran away from Virus Land. He was already dreaming about the sweet success story he was going to be when he went back home.

He travelled far and wide and finally reached his destination – Organ Land. Organ Land was populated with, well, organs. Its leaders were Eyes, Hands, Nose, Mouth, Heart, and their only mission was to protect delicate Lungs.

News of Clingy’s arrival stirred fear in Organ Land. They could imagine hear his evil laugh echo through its borders and the organs trembled with fear.

“This is going to be a big problem! How can we prevent this virus from entering Organ Land?” Nose fearfully said.

How are we going to survive this battle?!” said Mouth. “We must protect Lungs. She is not going to survive this attack.”

Sam the Soap said, “Don’t worry, that virus has no power over us!” All of them got to work.

Anthony the Alcohol told Hands, “Don’t touch anything! You must keep yourself clean.”

Sam the Soap said, “Nose, always sneeze in a tissue, that way your droplets do not spread.”

Sam the Soap and Anthony the Alcohol told Mouth, “Always drink water and eat fruits and vegetables!”

Hands could not keep still. He wanted to touch things, to reach out and to hug his friends. Hands said, “I can’t stand this anymore! It’s too hard for me to follow!”

Anthony the Alcohol and Sam the Soap called in their other cleaner friends. Everyone assembled their gear and prepared for battle.They were instructed to close all the borders to prevent the hideously destructive virus from entering Organ Land. Anthony the Alchohol said, “Here we are, lets hurry!”

As they went to the borders, they bumped into the ugly looking creature. Clingy said, “Well, who do we have here?” Sam the Soap exclaimed, “So you are the terrible virus the organs were talking about!” Clingy replied, "The one and only SARS CoV-2! "

The cleaners fought Clingy using their disinfecting weapons. Clingy was strong though, and it was a hard fight. The cleaners were trapped but they needed to make sure Clingy did not get through. They had to protect Lungs.“We have no choice but to fight him,” Anthony the Alcohol said. When Clingy landed on Hands, he began to climb, but he was not able to stay there for long. Hands shouted, "Anthony, I need you!” Anthony the Alcohol fired 70 %isopropyl alcohol bullets from the top of his head. “Sam! I need backup!” he screamed.

Sam the Soap rushed to their defense with his powerful disinfectants spewing killer bubbles from his slippery body. Clingy retreated. He was drenched in the decontaminators’ powerful artillery. He fell backward, weakened, defeated. He was going to have to find another land to invade.

Clingy ran out of Organ Land sobbing hard. The Bureau of Skins, the police of Organ Land, captured him and tossed him out of their epidermal gates. Clingy was dejected. He started his miserable trek back home. His family received him at the gates and spoke with him. "Clingy, we cannot defeat the organs. We need to stay in Virus Land where we belong. They will always find a way to fight us."

The Organs in Organ Land lived a happy and squeaky clean life ever after and Lungs continued to reign supreme. “Remember to wash your hands and keep clean!” - The Organs

title: Smart Tactics
content:
Mora kept glancing at the clock on the wall. It was getting late! She had to finish all her chores and leave for practice at once. She couldn’t be late again!

Hooray, finished at last! Washing the dishes was Mora’s last chore of the day. It was time to go to the field! However…

“What happened here?” Mora wondered, annoyed. She saw tanks, helicopters, and toy soldiers scattered on the floor.

Her younger twin siblings, Togi and Roma, had made a mess in their room. Dirty clothes were hanging from the basket. Mora stomped her feet.

Mora quickly picked up their mess. She gathered everything into a basket. She would have to clean it up after practice.

She looked at the time. It was almost half past three! Mora said goodbye to Mom. She had to run to get to practice on time.

Crash… ouch!The slippery road caused Mora to fall. Her knee was in terrible pain. Even so, she had to get back up.

Just as Mora worried, she arrived late again. Her friends had finished warming up. Even when dribbling the ball, Mora couldn’t concentrate. The ball slipped away from her over and over.

This couldn’t happen again! How could she get the twins to clean up after themselves? All they thought about was playing soldiers. Wait, soldiers!

"There’s got to be a way to get the two little soldiers to clean," thought Mora. "Togi, Roma. Do you guys want to play soldiers?” Mora asked, beginning to execute her plan. The twins immediately exclaimed, “Yes we do!"

“Attention!” Mora ordered. The twins immediately stood up. “Troops! Your first mission is independence. Wake up, fold your blankets, and make your beds by yourselves. Dismissed!”

The twins moved while shouting, “Spread the blanket. One step forward. One, two, fold!” Mora tried to hide her laughter.

“The next mission is agility! Clean up your toys within 10 minutes. Ready? On your mark, get set, go!” Mora instructed.

The twins were back in action. The toys were cleaned up in time. Mission accomplished!

“Hey, there are some cakes in the basket!” Roma and Togi exclaimed. “Surprise! It’s a reward for your agility, soldiers,” said Mora. “Thank you, Mora!”

After a quick break, their next mission was cautiousness! “Clean the room of dust and dirt! Don’t leave one speck behind,” Mora ordered. “Understood!” the twins replied.

Wow, their room and the living room were spotless now.

The twins' military-like training took place every day. They memorized the sequence of tasks by the code independence, agility, and cautiousness. The twins were happy to be soldiers. Mora was relieved some weight was taken off her shoulders.

Wow, now Mora could come to practice on time. She wouldn't be late again.

Wait, but why were Togi and Roma waiting in front of Mora’s room? “Where are you two going?” Mora asked. “We want to come with you to practice. We want to learn strength!” they said excitedly.

Wait a minute. The troop commander had to perform an inspection first. Great! How neat!

“Thank you, troops. Remember to say goodbye to Mom before you leave.Dismissed!” Mora directed.“Copy that!” the twins replied.

At practice, Mora dribbled the ball with ease. She smiled when she saw her twin siblings cheering on the sidelines.

title: An ice cream trade
content:
"Nyam nyam... This ice cream is so yummy!"

"Nana, Nini! Let me have a bite of your ice cream!"

"No way! Blehhh..."

"Alright. I've got something even cooler than your ice cream."

"Woah! So beautiful! I want to try it. Can you hold this ice cream for me?" Sure, give it to me."

"Puff puff puff... Bubbles bubbles up up up..."

"I want to try too."

"Can you hold this ice cream for me, brother?"Nini trusted Tip with her ice cream and ran to join Nana.

"Nana, we run out of bubbles.""So let's get our ice cream back."

"Tip, where did all our ice cream go?"

"My bubbles are used up, so your ice cream is gone too!... Hehehe." - Tip chuckled"So we have nothing to play now."

"Why not? We still have Tuntun here! Let's go play with Tuntun!" "Tuntun, Tuntun! Come here, come here now!"And then the kids spent all the rest of the afternoon playing with Tuntun.

title: I Will Change the World
content:
Layla's grandpa had invented a distinguished new car. She was so proud to be there when he received a special award for it.

On the way home, Layla asked him all about his marvelous invention. "What makes it so special? Can it fly or drive super fast?"

He laughed, and said, "No, dear. What makes this car unique is that it solves problems! Instead of gasoline, it runs on water. If more people drive cars like this, we can reduce the harmful gases in our atmosphere and maybe stop the climate change that is happening to our planet."

"But what is climate change? Why do we need to stop it?" Layla asked.

"It started with the industrial revolution. New machinery and factories caused a lot of pollution to be released. So much carbon dioxide was put into the atmosphere that it created a hole in Earth's ozone layer. The ozone layer protects the earth from the sun. The ozone hole means more heat from the sun gets into our atmosphere, changing the climate around the world."

Layla could not stop thinking about how our planet was being harmed. She was sure she could help to change things, just like her Grandpa. "I'm going to stop climate change!" she told her brother.But he just laughed. "You're only a kid. You can't make any difference!"

At school, she told all of her classmates about her ideas. But they did not listen either.

Layla was almost ready to give up, before she had even started. Her grandpa noticed her sad face and came to talk with her."Failure," he told her, "is the first step to success. You must still believe in your dream, even if it is difficult at first."

He encouraged Layla to share her idea with more people than those she knew in her town."I can use social media to share my ideas with the world!""Now you're thinking," Grandpa said with a smile.

Soon, her classmates came to ask her about the posts they had seen online. They were amazed how many people had responded to Layla's ideas."You can help too!" Layla told them. "When we work together, we can achieve anything."

Soon everyone in Layla's community wanted to help. They decided to plant more trees to help remove carbon dioxide and purify the air.

People also learned how easy it was to save energy in their homes with just a few changes!

Even Layla's brother decided to help by riding his bike instead of getting a ride in the car from his parents.

A few months later, Layla received a special award from her principal. Her entire community was proud of the hard work she had done to help change the world.

Layla knew one person would be more proud than anyone else."Thank you Grandpa!" she shouted into the microphone. "Thank you for reminding me to never give up."

THE END

title: Lara’s Stories
content:
Lara lives in a small village that is far from any large city. Everyone lives just as they have for hundreds of years. Nothing ever changes, and most people are happy to keep things the way they are.But Lara is a curious girl. She wants to know everything and dreams of learning about the world outside her village.

Lara reads all the books in her home. When she finishes those, she reads all the books at school, then she reads all the books in the public library. And still, she wants to know more! In her entire village there aren't enough books to quench Lara’s curiosity.

Then, one day Lara travels with her father to sell produce at the market, and there something very curious happens.

A strange-looking man approaches Lara. His face and hair are white as flour and his nose and cheeks are red like tomatoes. His eyes are as blue as the sky. The man looks at the tomatoes and says, "How much is the tomato?" in a foreign language.

Lara shrugs her shoulders to show the man she does not understand. But then, he pulls a strange device out of his pocket. He taps on it with his finger, then says to her in a way she can understand, "How much are the tomatoes?"

Lara is amazed that the man could learn to speak to her with just a glance at this device! He explains that the device is a mobile phone which connects him to all the information he could ever want to know. He shows her a dictionary, pictures, and stories on the screen.

For the rest of the day, all Lara can think about is the device and how amazing it would be to have something that could answer all her questions! As she prepares to go home with her father at the end of the day, she sees an advertisement in one of the empty produce crates.

It is a picture of a mobile phone. the same one the man had! "Limited Offer!" she reads. "You can buy this phone for only 10 0p ounds. But this price is only good until the end of the month!"

On their way home, Lara shows her father the advertisement. She enthusiastically asks him, "Can we buy it?"

"No, Lara. We must use all our savings to fix the ceiling of our home." But Lara is determined to find a way.

The next morning, Lara asks her neighbor Martin for a job. "Would you hire me to keep an eye on your sheep?" Martin hates being a shepherd, so he says yes straight away.

Lara takes the sheep to the pasture, and sits down to watch over them. Then she starts to read a book. She dives into the story and soon forgetes about the sheep. She doesn't notice when they all scatter away.

When Martin comes back at sunset, he is upset to find only two sheep left. Lara and Martin spend the rest of the night collecting lost sheep."I will not pay you for losing my sheep," Martin says to Lara once the sheep are all safely returned."I am sorry," Lara says. "I will find another job."

The next day, Lara decides to start a garden. She will grow vegetables to sell, just like her father! But would they grow quickly enough to sell before the offer ends?

A couple of weeks later, Lara harvests her vegetables. Her father takes her to the market to sell them.

At the end of the day, only two radishes that were stuck together remain in Lara's boxes. A man stops by and asks her why they are stuck.

Lara thinks for a moment, then says, "The radishes' mother left to visit her aunt and never returned. Their father got married to a beautiful new radish and did not spend time with them anymore. Since that day, the two radishes decided to stick together forever."The man laughs and gives her half a pound for the radishes. Then he gives her five pounds for the interesting story!

But when she gets home and counts her money, Lara realizes that she has earned only 50 pounds. Her father tries to cheer her up. "I blame those radishes," he says with a smile. "You know what they say, there is nothing cheaper than radishes!"

There is only one week left for Lara to earn enough money to buy the mobile phone. She thinks hard about what she could do to earn more money. There is not enough time to grow more vegetables, and she knows she is not good at watching sheep. Then she remembers the man who gave her money for the story about the radishes!

The next day after school, she puts a chair in the middle of the yard and makes an announcement. "I am going to stand here and tell stories every day after school. If you want to attend, the cost is one pound."

On the first day, only three of her friends come. The second day is also quiet, and the third day as well. But on the fourth day . . .

. . . it seems her entire village has come to hear Lara's stories!By the end of the week, Lara has earned enough money to buy the mobile phone.

Lara has never been so excited as the day her father takes her to the market to buy the phone.

Would it change her life? Would she come to know everything? Maybe, or maybe not. But now that Lara knows how to work hard to get what she dreams of, anything is possible.

The end

title: Ekbitte: The Boy Who Could Fit in the Palm of a Hand
content:
A long time ago, a poor old man lived in a village. He had no children. The old man had a cucumber plant in his garden. Though the plant had very lush vines and flowers, only one cucumber grew.

The cucumber was very small. Only the size of a human hand. This made the old man very angry. “May the woman who eats this cucumber have a baby of this very size!” he said angrily.

One day a woman from the neighborhood sneaked into the old man's garden. She saw the cucumber. She picked the cucumber and ate it up.

The woman became pregnant after eating the cucumber. Nine months later, she gave birth to a son. The baby was tiny. As the child got older, he did not grow much taller.The mother was very worried.

Seeing the size of his body, people called the boy Ekbitte since he could fit in the palm of a hand.When Ekbitte was eleven years old, he said to his mother, "Mother, I want to help you with the chores." "How on earth can you help me, son?" the mother asked. She was tired from working so hard. "Let me try, and see it for yourself,” Ekbitte replied. *ekbitte means palm-sized in the Nepali language.

"All right then. Bring some straw in from the threshing ground. The buffalo is hungry," his mother said. She didn't believe that Ekbitte could do it. After a while, Ekbitte shouted from the courtyard. "Mother, I have brought the straw. Where do you want me to put it?"

"Put it in front of the buffalo,” his mother shouted from inside the house. "The buffalo will not be able to eat all the straw that I have brought with me. Perhaps you should come out and show me where I can store it?" Ekbitte shouted. His mother sighed. "Oh boy. You brought a few strands of straw and now you are causing an uproar."

When Ekbitte’s mother came outside, she was surprised to see how much straw was lying on the threshing floor. “What kind of magic is this?” his mother exclaimed. Despite his size, Ekbitte was very strong.

From then on, Ekbitte did all the household chores by himself. His mother was very relieved. Her face looked brighter and happier every day.

A few years later, she noticed hair on her son’s upper lip. He was growing up. She came to him and said, "Son, you are grown up now. It is time for you to marry."So Ekbitte went off to look for a bride. On his way, he met a wild cat. He told her the reason for his journey. "Take me with you. I may be of use to you someday,” the wild cat said. "Yes, you can keep me company," Ekbitte said. And he pushed the wild cat into one of his ears.

A little further ahead, Ekbitte came across a fox. The fox wanted to come with Ekbitte, too. So Ekbitte pushed the fox into his other ear and moved on.

After walking some distance, Ekbitte came to the big Ganges River.. It was impossible for Ekbitte to cross it. "Oh Mother Ganga, please help me," he begged the river. Then, sucking all the water of the river into his ears, he continued on his way.

Ekbitte reached the big city. The king lived there. Ekbitte heard that he had a beautiful daughter. Ekbitte wanted to meet her. He headed toward the palace.

At the palace, Ekbitte greeted the king. "Your Majesty, I want to marry your daughter."This made the king angry. “How dare you ask such a thing?” the king shouted angrily. Then the king ordered his soldiers, “Shut him in the chicken coop. Let the chickens peck his body. They will teach him some manners.”

The soldiers pushed Ekbitte into the chicken coop. When the soldiers left, Ekbitte whispered to the wild cat, "Friend, I need your help.” The wild cat came out of Ekbitte’s ear and said, "What can I do for you, my friend?" “Could you please meow for me?” Ekbitte asked. The cat meows very loudly. The chickens were scared. They panicked and broke the coop apart. All the chickens run loose. After doing its job, the wild cat went back into Ekbitte’s ear. Ekbitte safely strutted out of the broken coop.

The next morning, when the king went outside, he found the coop broken and the chickens grazing outside. He also noticed that there were fewer chickens than the day before. Ekbitte was standing in front of him and smiling. The king was even angrier. He ordered his soldiers, "Throw him in the goat pen!" The soldiers threw Ekbitte in the pen and left. This time, Ekbitte asked the fox for help. The fox came out of Ekbitte’s ear and howled very loudly. The howling frightened the goats. They ran wild, causing the pen to fall apart. The goats ran free. After doing his job, the fox went back into Ekbitte’s ear.

The next day, the king went to inspect the goat pen. He was surprised to see that Ekbitte was safe and sound. This time, the king decided to throw Ekbitte into a fire. He ordered all the townspeople to collect dung cakes. They stacked them high in the center of the city. The soldiers set the dung cakes on fire.

As the soldiers threw Ekbitte into the fire, he prayed to the water, “Mother Ganga, could you please come out and help me?” A powerful jet of water gushed out of Ekbitte’s ear. It put out the fire in an instant.But even after the fire was over, the water continued to flow out of Ekbitte's ear. Soon, the city was almost completely underwater.

When the king saw that the city was about to sink, he panicked. "Oh Ekbitte, sir! I have made a mistake. You are clearly very strong and clever. Could you please stop the water from flowing?" Ekbitte said, "Your Majesty, for that to happen, you must give me your blessing to marry your daughter.” The king promised. Ekbitte said, "Mother Ganga, will you please return to my ear?" The water went back into Ekbitte's ear. The city was dry again.

The king was amazed. "You may be small, but you are impressive,” said the king. The princess also liked Ekbitte. The king gave his blessing to let Ekbitte and his daughter marry. Ekbitte invited his mother to the city for the wedding. The king married the princess and Ekbitte. Ekbitte became a prince. After the death of the king, Ekbitte became the king. He served the country and its people for a long time.

title: The Flower Hunt
content:
"Little Hummingbird, will you bring home some night-blooming jasmine for the nest?" Mother asked.

I went out to search for the night-blooming jasmine."Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the white lotus, Little Hummingbird," said Ladybug.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the dahlia, Little Hummingbird." said Butterfly.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the sunflower, Little Hummingbird," said Caterpillar.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the ground lily, Little Hummingbird," said Bee.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the poinsettia, Little Hummingbird," said Spider.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the night-blooming jasmine, Little Hummingbird," said Firefly."Just what I needed!" I said happily. "Thank you, Firefly."

"Well done, my Little Hummingbird! Now our nest looks very pretty," said Mother.

title: Take a Photo of Me, Too!
content:
“Our class is taking part in a photography competition. To win a prize you need to take a really good group photo. Remember, professional photographers will be judging the photos,” the teacher told the class.

Veera and Cool left class together. "You go that way. I'll go this way. We can meet tomorrow to share our photos,” Veera said.

Veera met some zebras. “You look beautiful, I'll take a good picture of you,” she said and made them stand in order. "Take a picture of me as well," Crow shouted, swooping in. "Us too, us too!’ the baby crows chirped. “No, I don’t want you all in my picture,” shouted Veera.

Cool saw a turtle and asked, "Mr. Turtle, I want to take a good picture. Can you pose for me?" Crow swooped down and shouted, "Picture? Take a picture of me as well." “Sure, come with me,” Cool said.

These are young tigers. I can take a good picture of them, Veera thought. "Stand in order,” she commanded.Right at the moment Giraffe came and asked, "Can you take a picture of me too?" “Ugh, all of you won’t fit!" Veera said angrily.

Meanwhile, Cool went searching for Peacock and Lion. He also met Zebra. He requested them all to come to one pose together for his photo.

He invited Hopping Deer. He went searching for Rat. He invited high flying Eagle as well. Cool also welcomed Giraffe who came asking "Can you take a picture of me too?"

As they all gathered for the photo, a competition started about who would stand in the first row. They started fighting, pushing and pulling each other.

Suddenly Cool said, "Take a picture of me!" The fight stopped as Cool entered the group. Everyone turned towards him.

"Okay, now stand in the area that I point to," Cool directed. Cool organized everyone and took a good picture. "Thank you all for being in my photo."

Who do you think won the competition? Take a look!

title: Count your Chickens
content:
Meena is a little girl who lives in a village with her parents, her grandmother, her brother Raju, and her baby sister Rani. Mithu, the parrot, is her best friend.In many ways, Meena is like any other little girl you know, but, in some ways, she is completely different.Join in Meena’s adventures as she laughs, climbs trees, asks questions, solves problems, and shows you all the things a little girl can do.

One day, Meena and Mithu were returning home after collecting firewood.

They had to pass the village school on the way. Raju went to this school. Meena and Mithu decided to stop at the school and see what was happening.

They found the teacher telling the children a wonderful story.

Meena and Mithu liked the story so much that they stayed and listened to the story till the very end. Meena wished she could go to school too.

Walking back home, Meena pretended that she was a teacher and that Mithu was her student. She taught the parrot to say his name.

When Meena got home, Raju was proudly telling their father about all the things he learnt at school.

Meena looked at their father. "Father, why can’t I go to school, too?" she asked.

"You are needed at home to help your mother," said her father. "Girls only need to learn how to cook, clean, and look after the house," added her mother. "You don’t need to go to school for that!"

Poor Meena! That night, she stood sadly at the window. The school building was shining in the moonlight. How she wished she could study!

When she finally fell asleep, Meena had a strange dream. She was in a classroom with many other girls and boys—and Mithu was their teacher!

The next morning, Meena watched sadly as Raju and his friends went to school.

She remembered her dream and sat down to think. Somehow, she must make it come true. But how?

Then Meena had a wonderful idea: she would send Mithu to school, and he could come back and teach her everything he learnt there.

Mithu sat all morning at the window of the classroom. He listened carefully as the teacher taught the 2- times table.

He then flew back home and taught Meena…

… Two ones are two.Two twos are four.Two threes are six…Soon, Meena was counting six of everything she saw.

She kept counting her father’s six chickens. Meena was finally learning arithmetic, just like Raju.

That afternoon, when Meena and Mithu were busy, a thief came creeping up the wall. He stole one of the chickens and ran off.

"Six grains," counted Meena,"… and six chickens." She turned to count them once more, but there was one missing.

Meena was puzzled. She looked all around, and that’s when she saw the thief running away. "Thief, thief!" shouted Meena, as she and Mithu ran after him.

Soon, half the village had joined the chase.

"Thief, thief," squawked Mithu into the thief’s ear. The man was so scared that he fell backward into the paddy field.

And there he stayed until the villagers came running up.

The village headman was very proud of Meena. He asked her how she had noticed the thief, and Meena explained that she had counted the chickens and found one missing.

The headman then congratulated Meena’s parents for sending such a clever girl to school. When Meena’s parents said that Meena did not go to school, the villagers were amazed. "Every child should go to school," said the headman.

"Yes," said a neighbor. "My married daughter lives far away, but she can write me letters because I sent her to school.""My educated daughter runs her own poultry business," said an old woman, proudly. "I went to school, and I can look after my baby better," added a shy, young mother.

Meena’s parents made a big decision. They decided that Meena would start school the very next day.

Meena and Raju were overjoyed. They danced with happiness.

Everyone was still puzzled about one thing: who had taught Meena to count? "A friend," said Meena and giggled as Mithu announced proudly, "My name is Mithu!"

The next day was Meena’s first day at school. She was very happy. She had caught a chicken thief and made her dream come true!

Meena and Mithu say, "Every child must go to school!"

Print this puzzle and solve it by placing the point of your pencil on dot number 1 and drawing a line to dot number 2. Then draw another line to dot number 3, and so on, until you have connected all the dots. After you have done this, you may use your crayons to color this surprise picture.
